passages.text: “Indeed, my eyes have seen all this; my ears have heard and understood.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job addresses his friends.
Job says he has seen everything they mention.
Job says his eyes have witnessed all these things.
Job says his ears have heard these things.
Job says he has understood what he heard.
passages.original: הֶן־ כֹּ֭ל רָאֲתָ֣ה עֵינִ֑י שָֽׁמְעָ֥ה אָ֝זְנִ֗י וַתָּ֥בֶן לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
passages.sermon: Job speaks to his friends.\r\nJob says he knows what they know.\r\nJob says he is not inferior to them.
passages.original: כְּֽ֭דַעְתְּכֶם יָדַ֣עְתִּי גַם־ אָ֑נִי לֹא־ נֹפֵ֖ל אָנֹכִ֣י מִכֶּֽם׃

passages.text: Yet I desire to speak to the Almighty and argue my case before God.
passages.sermon:
Job is the speaker.
Job wants to speak to the Almighty.
Job wants to present his case before God.
Job desires to argue directly with God.
passages.original: אוּלָ֗ם אֲ֭נִי אֶל־ שַׁדַּ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְהוֹכֵ֖חַ אֶל־ אֵ֣ל אֶחְפָּֽץ׃

passages.text: You, however, smear with lies; you are all worthless physicians.
passages.sermon:
You are my friends.
You tell lies.
You cover things with falsehoods.
You act like doctors.
You cannot heal anyone.
You are all useless as physicians.
passages.original: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם אַתֶּ֥ם טֹֽפְלֵי־ שָׁ֑קֶר רֹפְאֵ֖י אֱלִ֣ל כֻּלְּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
He says, "If only you would stay silent."
"That would show you have wisdom."
passages.original: מִֽי־ יִ֭תֵּן הַחֲרֵ֣שׁ תַּחֲרִישׁ֑וּן וּתְהִ֖י לָכֶ֣ם לְחָכְמָֽה׃

passages.text: Hear now my argument, and listen to the plea of my lips.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
He asks them to listen to him.
He says, "Hear my argument."
He says, "Pay attention to my words."
He wants them to listen carefully to his plea.
passages.original: שִׁמְעוּ־ נָ֥א תוֹכַחְתִּ֑י וְרִב֖וֹת שְׂפָתַ֣י הַקְשִֽׁיבוּ׃

passages.text: Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf or speak deceitfully for Him?
passages.sermon:
God is holy.
God is just.
Do not speak wickedly for God.
Do not speak lies for God.
Do not defend God with false words.
Do not use deceit to support God.
passages.original: הַ֭לְאֵל תְּדַבְּר֣וּ עַוְלָ֑ה וְ֝ל֗וֹ תְּֽדַבְּר֥וּ רְמִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: Would you show Him partiality or argue in His defense?
passages.sermon:
God is holy and just.
God does not show favoritism.
Will you show God partiality?
Will you argue in God's defense?
God does not need you to defend Him.
God judges fairly.
God sees all things.
passages.original: הֲפָנָ֥יו תִּשָּׂא֑וּן אִם־ לָאֵ֥ל תְּרִיבֽוּן׃

passages.text: Would it be well when He examined you? Could you deceive Him like a man?
passages.sermon:
God is all-knowing.
God examines people.
Would it be good for you if God examined you?
You cannot deceive God.
You can deceive other people.
You cannot deceive God as you deceive a man.
passages.original: הֲ֭טוֹב כִּֽי־ יַחְקֹ֣ר אֶתְכֶ֑ם אִם־ כְּהָתֵ֥ל בֶּ֝אֱנ֗וֹשׁ תְּהָתֵ֥לּוּ בֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Surely He would rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality.
passages.sermon:
God sees everything.
\r\nGod knows your actions.
\r\nIf you secretly show partiality, God will know.
\r\nGod will rebuke you if you do this.
passages.original: הוֹכֵ֣חַ יוֹכִ֣יחַ אֶתְכֶ֑ם אִם־ בַּ֝סֵּ֗תֶר פָּנִ֥ים תִּשָּׂאֽוּן׃

passages.text: Would His majesty not terrify you? Would the dread of Him not fall upon you?
passages.sermon:
God is majestic.
God is powerful.
His majesty can terrify you.
His dread can fall upon you.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֣א שְׂ֭אֵתוֹ תְּבַעֵ֣ת אֶתְכֶ֑ם וּ֝פַחְדּ֗וֹ יִפֹּ֥ל עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.
passages.sermon:
You speak wise sayings.
Your sayings are like proverbs.
Your proverbs are made of ashes.
You try to protect yourselves.
Your defenses are weak.
Your defenses are made of clay.
passages.original: זִֽ֭כְרֹנֵיכֶם מִשְׁלֵי־ אֵ֑פֶר לְגַבֵּי־ חֹ֝֗מֶר גַּבֵּיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Be silent, and I will speak. Then let come to me what may.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
He asks them to be silent.
He says, "Let me speak."
He is ready for anything that may happen to him.
passages.original: הַחֲרִ֣ישׁוּ מִ֭מֶּנִּי וַאֲדַבְּרָה־ אָ֑נִי וְיַעֲבֹ֖ר עָלַ֣י מָֽה׃

passages.text: Why do I put myself at risk and take my life in my own hands?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job suffers greatly.
Job asks a question.
Why do I put myself in danger?
Why do I risk my own life?
Why do I take my life into my own hands?
passages.original: עַל־ מָ֤ה׀ אֶשָּׂ֣א בְשָׂרִ֣י בְשִׁנָּ֑י וְ֝נַפְשִׁ֗י אָשִׂ֥ים בְּכַפִּֽי׃

passages.text: Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.
passages.sermon:
Job is the speaker.
\r\nJob suffers greatly.
\r\nGod allows Job’s suffering.
\r\nJob says, “Even if God kills me, I will still trust Him.”
\r\nJob says, “I will defend my ways before God.”
passages.original: הֵ֣ן יִ֭קְטְלֵנִי לֹא אֲיַחֵ֑ל אַךְ־ דְּ֝רָכַ֗י אֶל־ פָּנָ֥יו אוֹכִֽיחַ׃

passages.text: Moreover, this will be my salvation, for no godless man can appear before Him.
passages.sermon:
God is holy and just.
No godless person can stand before God.
This truth gives me hope.
This truth will save me.
passages.original: גַּם־ הוּא־ לִ֥י לִֽישׁוּעָ֑ה כִּי־ לֹ֥א לְ֝פָנָ֗יו חָנֵ֥ף יָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: Listen carefully to my words; let my declaration ring in your ears.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job asks them to listen.
Job says, “Listen carefully to my words.”
Job says, “Let my declaration ring in your ears.”
passages.original: שִׁמְע֣וּ שָׁ֭מוֹעַ מִלָּתִ֑י וְ֝אַֽחֲוָתִ֗י בְּאָזְנֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Behold, now that I have prepared my case, I know that I will be vindicated.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job prepares his case.
Job stands ready to present his arguments.
Job knows he is righteous.
Job is confident God will declare him innocent.
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ נָ֭א עָרַ֣כְתִּי מִשְׁפָּ֑ט יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֥י אֶצְדָּֽק׃

passages.text: Can anyone indict me? If so, I will be silent and die.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks here.
Job is a righteous man who suffers greatly.
Job asks a question.
He says, "Who will contend with me?"
He means, "Can anyone accuse me?"
He says, "If someone can accuse me, I will be silent."
He says, "If I am silent, I will die."
passages.original: מִי־ ה֭וּא יָרִ֣יב עִמָּדִ֑י כִּֽי־ עַתָּ֖ה אַחֲרִ֣ישׁ וְאֶגְוָֽע׃

passages.text: Only grant these two things to me, so that I need not hide from You: Withdraw Your hand from me, and do not let Your terror frighten me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job asks God for two things.
Job says, “Do not do these two things to me.”
If God grants this, Job will not hide from God.
Job asks God to take His hand away from him.
Job asks God not to let His terror frighten him.
passages.original: אַךְ־ שְׁ֭תַּיִם אַל־ תַּ֣עַשׂ עִמָּדִ֑י אָ֥ז מִ֝פָּנֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א אֶסָּתֵֽר׃ כַּ֭פְּךָ מֵעָלַ֣י הַרְחַ֑ק וְ֝אֵ֥מָתְךָ֗ אַֽל־ תְּבַעֲתַֽנִּי׃

passages.text: Then call me, and I will answer, or let me speak, and You can reply.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job is suffering and feels accused by God.
Job asks God to call him.
Job promises to answer if God calls.
Job also asks for a chance to speak.
Job says God can reply if he speaks.
passages.original: וּ֭קְרָא וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ה אֽוֹ־ אֲ֝דַבֵּ֗ר וַהֲשִׁיבֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: How many are my iniquities and sins? Reveal to me my transgression and sin.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job asks about his sins.
Job says, “How many are my iniquities?”
Job says, “How many are my sins?”
Job asks God to show him his transgressions.
Job asks God to reveal his sin.
passages.original: כַּמָּ֣ה לִ֭י עֲוֺנ֣וֹת וְחַטָּא֑וֹת פִּֽשְׁעִ֥י וְ֝חַטָּאתִ֗י הֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Why do You hide Your face and consider me as Your enemy?
passages.sermon:
God, You are powerful and holy.
You hide Your face from me.
You treat me as Your enemy.
I do not understand why You do this.
passages.original: לָֽמָּה־ פָנֶ֥יךָ תַסְתִּ֑יר וְתַחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי לְאוֹיֵ֣ב לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Would You frighten a windblown leaf? Would You chase after dry chaff?
passages.sermon:
God, You are powerful and just.
I am weak and fragile.
A windblown leaf is light and helpless.
Dry chaff is worthless and easily scattered.
Would You frighten a windblown leaf?
Would You chase after dry chaff?
passages.original: הֶעָלֶ֣ה נִדָּ֣ף תַּעֲר֑וֹץ וְאֶת־ קַ֖שׁ יָבֵ֣שׁ תִּרְדֹּֽף׃

passages.text: For You record bitter accusations against me and bequeath to me the iniquities of my youth.
passages.sermon:
God, You write down bitter charges against me.
You keep a record of my pain.
You give me the sins I committed when I was young.
You make me bear the guilt of my youth.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תִכְתֹּ֣ב עָלַ֣י מְרֹר֑וֹת וְ֝תוֹרִישֵׁ֗נִי עֲוֺנ֥וֹת נְעוּרָֽי׃

passages.text: You put my feet in the stocks and stand watch over all my paths; You set a limit for the soles of my feet.
passages.sermon: God puts my feet in the stocks.\r\nGod watches all my paths.\r\nGod marks out a boundary for the soles of my feet.
passages.original: וְתָ֘שֵׂ֤ם בַּסַּ֨ד׀ רַגְלַ֗י וְתִשְׁמ֥וֹר כָּל־ אָרְחוֹתָ֑י עַל־ שָׁרְשֵׁ֥י רַ֝גְלַ֗י תִּתְחַקֶּֽה׃

passages.text: So man wastes away like something rotten, like a moth-eaten garment.
passages.sermon: Man is weak and mortal.\r\nHe wastes away like something rotten.\r\nHe decays like a garment eaten by moths.
passages.original: וְ֭הוּא כְּרָקָ֣ב יִבְלֶ֑ה כְּ֝בֶ֗גֶד אֲכָ֣לוֹ עָֽשׁ׃
